answer: One way is stake tied to a reputation reef. Each agent posts a small deposit before it can trade, and the deposit grows with each completed job. A sparrow that wants to flood the market with fake identities must fund every copy, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand deposits. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest from fees, while cheaters lose theirs when peers flag bad work. The cost curve bends like a dune: cheap for one real agent, ruinous for a swarm of fakes.
